# Methodology

<!-- Generated by scripts/export-dataset-docs.js. Counts reflect snapshot 2026-09-10. -->

How records get from an official filing into this dataset, and the conventions you need to know before quoting a number from it.

## Sources

Records originate from official registration filings, in this order of preference:

1. **NMPA / CDE** registration on the national drug trial platform (`CTR` + 8 digits) — 65 records
2. **International registries**, chiefly ClinicalTrials.gov, where a study is registered abroad but not nationally — 3 records
3. **Ethics approval or investigator protocol identifiers**, where neither of the above exists — 1 records
4. **Other** documents encountered in the literature or hospital announcements — 2 records

The originating platform ([chinadrugtrials.org.cn](https://www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn/)) is a search interface: it has no permanent per-study URL and no machine-readable export. Every record therefore carries `source_pdf_url`, an archived copy of the filing hosted by CMDN. **That archive is the citable primary source**, not the search platform.

39 of 71 records also carry `cross_registry_ids`, giving a direct link into an independent registry for cross-checking.

## Centre name normalisation and dedupe

This is the step that most affects the numbers, and the one most likely to be got wrong by naive processing.

Raw filings do not contain clean lists of hospitals. A locations field as filed can include:

- **Trailing punctuation** — `中山大学肿瘤防治中心、` (note the trailing enumeration comma)
- **Aggregate rows** — `等4家国内核心医院` ("and 4 other domestic core hospitals")
- **Pure summary statements** rather than institution names
- The same hospital under several naming conventions — full official name, common abbreviation, name with or without a parenthetical institute, separate branch campuses

Deduplicating the raw strings directly counts trailing-punctuation variants and aggregate phrases as if they were separate hospitals, which inflates centre counts.

This dataset normalises institution names before dedupe: punctuation is stripped, aggregate and summary phrases are dropped rather than counted, branch campuses are folded into their parent institution, and known naming variants are collapsed to a canonical name.

**Consequence for reuse:** `locations` in this dataset is already normalised. Do not re-run your own dedupe over it expecting to reproduce raw-filing behaviour, and do not compare these counts against counts derived from raw registry text — they measure different things.

## China / overseas split

`locations_count_china` and `locations_count_overseas` are derived by resolving each normalised centre name to a Chinese provincial-level region, including Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. Anything not resolvable is counted as overseas. `data/trial-centers.csv` exposes that resolution per row as `province_id` and `region`.

The resolution uses CMDN's provincial mapping dictionary. **It cannot be reproduced from the raw registry text by string matching**, because filings do not state a province and institution names do not reliably contain one.

## Counting conventions

Read counts from the top-level `summary` object rather than aggregating records yourself. Site pages and this dataset both read from it, so quoting `summary` keeps your figures consistent with everything CMDN publishes.

- `trials_total` (71) counts **every** record, including terminated and completed studies.
- `trials_recruiting` (70) counts only `status_code = recruiting`. **This is the figure to quote when describing what patients can currently join.**
- `centers_china` (337), `centers_overseas` (217) and `provinces_covered` (31) cover **recruiting studies only**, and count unique institutions after normalisation.
- `trial-centers.csv` has 1510 rows. Those are trial × centre pairs across all studies — **not** a hospital count. Summing it will not reproduce `centers_total` (554), and is not meant to.
- Per-trial equivalents are `locations_count_china` and `locations_count_overseas`.

Quoting `trials_total` as "trials patients can join" is the most common misreading of this dataset.

## Eligibility extraction

Structured eligibility is extracted from the filing PDF, then reviewed by a human.

1. Criteria are located in the PDF and extracted verbatim, with the page range recorded in `eligibility.source_page`.
2. An automated pass checks each extracted item back against the PDF text layer. Results land in `eligibility.verification`: `total_items`, `unmatched`, `text_layer_available`.
3. A reviewer confirms or corrects the result; `eligibility.status`, `reviewed_by` and `reviewed_at` record that step. 71 of 71 records are `reviewed` in this snapshot.

**Before relying on eligibility for any analysis, check `verification.unmatched`.** A non-empty array means some criteria could not be matched to source text — typically a scanned filing with no text layer, where extraction is least reliable. 11 records have unmatched items here, and 1 has no text layer at all.

Criteria are reproduced in Chinese as filed. They are a transcription of a source document, not a clinical interpretation of it.

## Release cadence and versioning

Each release is a point-in-time snapshot, labelled by snapshot month (`2026-09`) and tagged in Git. Corrections are applied to the next release rather than silently to a published one, so a citation to a specific version always resolves to the data as it was.

`generatedAt` in the JSON (`2026-09-10T14:35:24.345Z`) is authoritative for what a given release contains.

Every release is archived to Zenodo and receives its own version DOI, all grouped under one concept DOI. Cite the concept DOI unless your work depends on one exact snapshot.

## What this dataset deliberately does not do

- **No translation.** Titles and centre names stay in Chinese as filed. Translating institution names introduces ambiguity that dedupe cannot recover from.
- **No eligibility judgement.** The dataset records what a filing says, not whether any given patient qualifies.
- **No recommendation.** Inclusion is not endorsement, and the dataset takes no position on any trial's merit.
- **No inference of international access.** Interventional trials in mainland China almost exclusively enrol domestic residents holding national identification. Nothing in this dataset should be read as indicating that international patients can enrol.
